Question: For a stable system, what are the restrictions on the gain margin and phase margin?
A: Both gain margin and phase margin are negative
B: Gain margin is negative and phase margin is positive
C: Gain margin is positive and phase margin is negative
D: Both gain margin and phase margin are positive
Answer: Both gain margin and phase margin are positive
Explaination: A stable system must have both positive gain margin (GM > 1 or > 0 dB) and positive phase margin.

Question: Which one of the following statements is correct for gain margin and phase margin of two closed loop systems having loop function G(s)H(s) and e^(-s) G(s)H(s)?
A: Both gain and phase margin of the two systems will be identical
B: Both gain and phase margin of G(s)H(s) will be more
C: Gain margins of the two systems are the same but phase margin of G(s)H(s) will be more
D: Phase margins of the two systems are the same but gain margin of G(s)H(s) will be more
Answer: Gain margins of the two systems are the same but phase margin of G(s)H(s) will be more
Explaination: As per the book key: the delay e^(-s) has magnitude 1 (so the magnitude plot and gain crossover are unchanged) and only adds phase lag -ω rad. The extra lag reduces the phase margin of the delayed system, so G(s)H(s) has more phase margin. (Strictly the phase crossover frequency also shifts, so GM also changes in general; the book treats it as the same.)

Question: What is the gain margin of a system when the magnitude of the polar plot at phase crossover is 'a'?
Explaination: Gain margin GM = 1/|G(jωpc)| = 1/a (or -20 log a in dB).

Question: The Nyquist plot of the loop transfer function G(s)H(s) of a closed loop control system passes through the point (-1, j0) in the G(s)H(s) plane. The phase margin of the system is
Explaination: Passing through (-1, j0) means |G| = 1 at phase -180°, so PM = 180° + (-180°) = 0° (marginally stable).

Question: System is said to be marginally stable, if
A: Gain crossover frequency > Phase crossover frequency
B: Gain crossover frequency = Phase crossover frequency
C: Gain crossover frequency < Phase crossover frequency
D: Gain crossover frequency ≠ Phase crossover frequency
Answer: Gain crossover frequency = Phase crossover frequency
Explaination: Marginal stability means |G| = 1 and ∠G = -180° at the same frequency, i.e. ωgc = ωpc (GM = 0 dB, PM = 0°). ωgc < ωpc is stable and ωgc > ωpc is unstable.
